project-01.main_title: Building an AI-powered visa document generator to help travellers across the world.
project-01.intro_part1: The idea behind **visadocs.ai** began long before I ever considered building it, back when I was constantly frustrated by the paperwork involved in visa applications — both for myself and when helping my relatives.
project-01.intro_part2: I built the platform with a simple goal: to **streamline and simplify the visa application process.** Since requirements vary widely from one country to another, I decided to start with **travel itineraries**, as they are one of the most commonly required documents in visa applications.
project-01.intro_part3: Behind the scenes, it runs on a modern **React + Cloudflare stack**, integrates securely with **Stripe for payments**, and supports multilingual PDF generation. All generated PDFs are carefully **designed to meet typical embassy standards.**
project-01.specs_tools: Figma, OpenAI, Github, Git, Cloudflare, Brevo, EmailJS
project-01.specs_stack: React+Vite, Cloudflare, OpenAI API, Google Places API, Stripe Payments
project-01.objective_title: Offering a way to generate quality PDF travel itineraries in less than 2 minutes.
project-01.objective_intro: With many travel and visa-consultancy agencies offering tailored services, the idea was to build a **SaaS platform** which would be:

features.title: Product centred
features.content: A tool to simplify a complex part of the visa process.

features.title: Fast
features.content: Reducing time and stress during the visa demand process.

features.title: Quality focused
features.content: Serving top-tier PDFs that meet embassy format standards.

features.title: Global
features.content: Multi-language export to help users worldwide.

features.title: Single usage
features.content: You don’t apply for a visa every day, so no account is needed.

features.title: Affordable
features.content: A one-time, low-cost service to keep visa demand affordable.

project-01.process_title: POC → Low-fi design → Prototype & Tests → High-fi design → Final build
project-01.challenge_title: Where AI fell short. And why custom logic was needed.

challenge.intro_part1: When I started working on **visadocs.ai**, the idea was pretty clear in my mind. I would **leverage the power of AI to translate data from my front-end’s form into a well-constructed table.**
challenge.intro_part2: That table would feature, for each day of the travel itinerary **all the key information necessary**, and would include accurate data (no placeholder values).
challenge.blk1_part1: After some tests, I realised that itineraries **couldn’t be exported as PDFs**, nor could they **include real or accurate location data for the cities and hotels.**
challenge.blk1_part2: **Why?** When calling an AI model API directly, only the model’s “basic” reasoning layer is available. Anything more advanced **require using external APIs and libraries.**
challenge.blk2_part1: **Building the logic came piece by piece:** Integrating powerful APIs like Google Places API and REST API or using libraries like pdf-lib to turn complex JSON into clean, readable PDFs, and manually refining itineraries for multilingual use.
challenge.blk2_part2: The logic would have to be more complex and fragmented but also **more scalable and robust.**
challenge.outro_small: After the countless hours spent, I realised
challenge.outro_main: I took full ownership of the build, growing my skills with every step.

project-01.delivery_title: A scalable and robust system for quickly generating travel itineraries
project-01.delivery_par1: When I finally merged the <release> branch onto <master>, and after spending 20 minutes double-checking everything and doing QA on production, I was able to **sit back and contemplate what I’ve been building for the past six months.**
project-01.delivery_par2: This project went **beyond the scope of the usual job of a Product Designer**, I single-handedly built everything from scratch, from the very first scribble on a piece of paper to the last commit.
project-01.delivery_par3: There were **challenges at every step**, from design and development to infrastructure, security and even marketing. Above all, this project made me better at what counts:
project-01.delivery_outro: To 🏗 build and 🚀 ship web applications.

project-02.main_title: Creating a new identity and a fresh website for a visa consultancy agency.
project-02.intro_part1: In 2024, I returned to hands-on product design work after a period exploring a different craft. This project marked **my re-entry into digital product work**, where I partnered with **JMR Visa Services** to redesign their digital presence.
project-02.intro_part2: This project focused on transforming the online presence of **JMR Visa Services** into a clear, structured and credibility-driven experience. The goal was to turn the website into a **trust-building platform that converts visitors into qualified leads.**
project-02.intro_part3: **I owned the project end to end**, from brand refinement and UX strategy to visual design, front-end development (React), and Cloudflare-based hosting and deployment.
project-02.objective_title: Increase brand trust & convert visitors into qualified leads with a new website
project-02.objective_part1: When Jill approached me to redesign the brand identity and website for JMR Visa Services, the primary objective was clear: **establish trust online.** Her core customer base is **located in the Philippines**, where concerns about credibility and online scams strongly influence purchasing decisions.
project-02.objective_part2: Although the brand already had strong visibility across Facebook, Instagram and TikTok, **the website represented the main trust gap**. The project focused on creating a **professional, credibility-driven experience** that clearly explains services, reduces confusion around the visa process, and improves conversion through a structured quotation system.
project-02.process_title: A revamp articulated around modernity, accessibility and trust
project-02.process_part1: The strategy was to transform the website into a **conversion-focused trust platform**, not just a digital brochure. I began with a targeted brand refresh: simplifying the logo, refining the existing colours for better contrast and accessibility, and defining a consistent typographic hierarchy.
project-02.process_part2: Working closely with Jill, we clarified the tone of voice and restructured the information architecture. Each service was broken down into clear sections explaining **who it is for, what is included, and what is not**. Comparison tables and a structured page detailing the process were introduced to **reduce confusion and lower anxiety for first-time travellers.**
project-02.process_part3: Since prices are intentionally not displayed, the core conversion mechanism became a **quotation request form**. I implemented a structured front-end form connected to **EmailJS**, allowing Jill to **receive organised requests without building a complex backend system**. The result was **a lightweight but effective lead-generation setup**.
project-02.challenge_title: Designing trust in a market sensitive to scams
project-02.challenge_main_title: Building credibility through structure and social proof
project-02.challenge_part1: Unlike highly technical projects, the main challenge here was psychological: **how do you visually communicate that a consultancy is legitimate and trustworthy in a market where scams are common?**
project-02.challenge_part2: **The testimonial section became the most complex part of the build.** It needed to display real client photos and detailed feedback while remaining compact, modern and fully responsive. **Balancing long-form text, imagery and layout logic across devices required multiple iterations** before reaching a solution that felt both credible and approachable.
project-02.challenge_outro_small: This project reinforced an important lesson:
project-02.challenge_outro_main: Trust is not claimed — it is designed, structured and demonstrated.
project-02.delivery_title: A trust-driven and conversion-focused web platform
project-02.delivery_part1: The final website was fully designed and built using React and deployed on Cloudflare. It includes a refined brand identity, clear service architecture, structured comparison tables, a detailed visa process explanation, and a testimonial system featuring real client imagery.
project-02.delivery_part2: To further strengthen authority, I integrated educational YouTube content directly into the website. By showcasing immigration tips, guides and success stories, the platform bridges the gap between paid services and free value — reinforcing expertise and authenticity.
project-02.delivery_part3: More than a visual redesign, this project demonstrates my ability to translate business challenges into UX structure, design for trust in sensitive industries, and deliver complete, end-to-end web solutions.
project-02.delivery_outro: To 🏗 build trust-driven and 🚀 conversion-focused web platforms.

project-03.main_title: Leading the design of a feature facilitating conversations during live events.
project-03.intro_part1: The **Chat feature** was **born from a global shift in the events and conference landscape** during the 2020 **COVID-19** outbreak. Physical events like conferences and town halls drastically declined, while **digital events and online meetings rapidly expanded.**
project-03.intro_part2: As a result, **many of Pigeonhole Live’s core features had to be adapted**, as they were originally built for in-person experiences. During this period, much of my focus was on **product improvements and third-party integrations** with platforms such as Zoom, MS Teams or Webex.
project-03.intro_part3: The lack of physical presence and live audience feedback meant that **engagement was harder to grasp for event organisers** (Pigeonhole Live’s primary users). This gap led to the creation of the **Chat feature**, providing audiences with **a way to connect with both speakers and fellow attendees during digital and hybrid events.**
project-03.specs_tools: Figma, Github, Git, In-Browser Prototyping, Adobe After Effects
project-03.objective_title: Bridging the engagement gap in virtual events with real-time chat.
project-03.objective_part1: The goal of the Chat feature was to **introduce real-time audience interaction within virtual and hybrid events.**
project-03.objective_part2: By enabling attendees to **communicate during live sessions**, the feature aimed to **recreate the conversational dynamics of in-person events** and help organisers better understand and **foster audience engagement.**
project-03.process_title: Concept → Low-fi design → Live Prototype → High-fi design → First release

project-04.main_title: Imagining and designing a feature that brings the event audience’s emotions to life.
project-04.intro_part1: With the rapid rise of virtual events in 2020, many event organisers observed a **decline in audience engagement**. In particular, speakers often **struggled to gauge audience reactions**, making it harder to adapt their delivery and **maintain a strong connection with attendees.**
project-04.intro_part2: Lyon, the product owner at **Pigeonhole Live** then came to me with an open idea: **Find a fun and engaging way to keep attendees involved**, whether they were following a speaker on stage at a physical event or engaging through their mobile screens during virtual sessions
project-04.intro_part3: This led to the creation of **Reactions**. Inspired by existing live-streaming platforms, the feature initially **allowed attendees to react to video streams**. It then evolved to support reactions to Chat messages and replies, further **enhancing real-time interaction across the platform.**
project-04.specs_tools: Figma, Github, Git, In-Browser Prototyping, Adobe Photoshop, Adobe After Effects
